description: The Cropland Data Layer is the National Agricultural Statistics Service's annual, crop-specific land cover map of the United States, produced from satellite imagery. The 2025 CDL was released on 27 February 2026, and from 2024 the spatial resolution increased from 30 metres to 10 metres, with a 30 metre version still offered for consistency with the historical series; a Hawaii CDL for 2025 was released on 12 June 2026. Data are distributed through a national download page and the CroplandCROS web application, with metadata, FAQs, a CDL viewer, a Google Earth Engine based visualisation app (ACTIVE) and an ArcGIS StoryMap on the history of the programme; related NASS geospatial products include VegScape, crop condition and soil moisture layers, crop sequence boundaries and disaster analysis. Access is free; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the map is a classification of imagery, and the change to 10 metres in 2024 breaks the series unless the 30 metre version is used. For simulation it gives the location of crop types for hazard exposure of agriculture to floods, drought and heat, and for agricultural supply-chain scenarios. Related catalogue records include USDA NASS Quick Stats and JRC EUCROPMAP.
